description:
WHEN 13 at :247 - the second of the three ordered arms of EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :221-257 - reached by a key the file does not hold, and used here to prove that the FUNCTION UPPER-CASE normalisation at :132-134 is applied to the key the read is issued on and not only to the key that happens to match. The user id is typed entirely in lower case and matches no seeded row in either case form, so the read misses; the assertion of interest is therefore NOT the miss but the KEY THAT WAS USED, which the fingerprint carries as CDEMO-USER-ID. :132-134 is a single MOVE with two receivers - WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID - and the EXEC CICS READ at :211-219 addresses RIDFLD(WS-USER-ID), so the normalised eight characters in CDEMO-USER-ID are byte for byte the key the file was searched on. Pinning it at ZZZZ9999 while the request typed zzzz9999 is the whole point of this slot: a translation that keyed the read on the raw value would miss too and would still report 'User not found', so a case that asserted only the not-found result would pass on a broken translation. case12 makes the same ordering claim on a hit, where the typed key is mixed case and the row is found; together the two show the normalisation is applied before the read regardless of its outcome.

In source order: EVALUATE TRUE at :117-130 falls through to WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :128-129, because USERIDI is zzzz9999 and PASSWDI is password and neither is SPACES or LOW-VALUES; :132-134 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI) into WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID, turning zzzz9999 into ZZZZ9999 - UPPER-CASE folds lower-case alphabetics only, so the four digits pass through in place; :135-136 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(PASSWDI) into WS-USER-PWD, turning password into PASSWORD; :138 finds NOT ERR-FLG-ON, because nothing on this path has raised the flag from the SET ERR-FLG-OFF of :75, and performs READ-USER-SEC-FILE; the read at :211-219 offers ZZZZ9999 at the KEYLENGTH of :216, which is the whole eight-byte SEC-USR-ID span, and reports DFHRESP(NOTFND).

Exactly one read is issued, the one at :211-219, and it returns no record. Both halves of that are stated positively rather than left to be inferred: no row of USRSEC carries a decoded field set here, because a record that was never returned has no fields to diff - which is the opposite of case16, where the row the key addressed is pinned by all six of its named fields. WS-RESP-CD is 13, the raw numeric literal the source writes at :247 and the value common/FileStatus.java names NOTFND and FileStatus.fromCicsResp maps onto FileStatus.Outcome.NOT_FOUND. The arm is reached from the seeded data alone, so forcedOutcomes is empty: only case11 forces an outcome, and only because its WHEN OTHER at :252-256 is unreachable from any arrangement of well-formed rows. The lookup is a key-sequenced match on SEC-USR-ID at its full declared width, so a key differing only in case finds nothing - which is precisely why the miss cannot carry the assertion on its own and why the key is pinned instead.

The arm body at :248-251 is asserted statement by statement. :248 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, so the flag reads 'Y' on this path - unlike the wrong-password ELSE at :241-246, which moves the message and the cursor and sets no flag at all, an asymmetry case14 pins in detail and which is preserved rather than harmonised. :249 moves the twenty-nine-character literal 'User not found. Try again ...' into WS-MESSAGE. :250 moves -1 into USERIDL, which is how COBOL positions the cursor, so the cursor request names the user-id field and not the password field: USERIDL is the symbolic map's xxxL length item and is carried as validation and highlight metadata, never as a payload member, and no PASSWDL request is made anywhere on this path. :251 performs SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN.

No role and no transfer. :230-240 is inside the WHEN 0 arm and is never reached, so the response names no program at all - neither the admin target of :232 nor the regular-user target of :237 - and the two literals appear nowhere in this case. The communication area is where the statelessness is asserted: of the sixteen CARDDEMO-COMMAREA fields of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44, exactly one is written on this path, CDEMO-USER-ID, by the unconditional :132-134 that sits outside the EVALUATE above it. CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, CDEMO-USER-TYPE and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT are NOT populated, because :224-228 belongs to the signing-on path; the remaining eleven fields - the customer identifier and the three names, the account identifier and status, the card number, the two TO- fields and the last map and mapset - pass through untouched and are pinned as such. All of it arrives in the payload and leaves in the payload; nothing is held in a session, so the client can re-send the area to CC00 and continue the conversation.

SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN is performed, so the map is transmitted and the full eleven-item projection of mapset COSGN00 applies, at the widths app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY declares for its xxxI items: TRNNAMEO X(4) CC00, TITLE01O X(40), CURDATEO X(8), PGMNAMEO X(8) COSGN00C, TITLE02O X(40), CURTIMEO X(9), APPLIDO X(8), SYSIDO X(8), USERIDO X(8), PASSWDO X(8) and ERRMSGO X(78). This is the case in which the raw-versus-normalised asymmetry is directly observable on a re-sent screen, which cases 12 and 13 cannot show because neither path transmits the map: USERIDO carries the raw lower-case zzzz9999 and PASSWDO the raw lower-case password, while CDEMO-USER-ID in the very same response carries the normalised ZZZZ9999. The reason is the map's storage model - app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:85 declares 01 COSGN0AO REDEFINES COSGN0AI, and within each field the input view's xxxL plus xxxF plus four-byte FILLER occupies exactly the bytes the output view spends on a three-byte FILLER plus xxxC, xxxP, xxxH and xxxV, so xxxI and xxxO name the same storage at the same width. No paragraph of COSGN00C moves anything into USERIDO or PASSWDO, and the normalised values went into WORKING-STORAGE and were never written back, so what those two items hold at SEND time is the transmitted image. The echo is not normalised and the key is: both preservations are deliberate, and neither may be tidied into the other.

Byte-exact literals. The message path is the twenty-nine-character literal at :249 into WS-MESSAGE, which app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:38 declares PIC X(80), and then :149 moves WS-MESSAGE into ERRMSGO, which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:152 declares PIC X(78) - an alphanumeric MOVE to a narrower receiver, so the two rightmost characters are truncated off the RIGHT and the pinned image is the literal followed by forty-nine spaces, seventy-eight characters in all. It is the not-found text and not the wrong-password text, which is the same length and a different string. The two titles come from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy: CCDA-TITLE01 is '      AWS Mainframe Modernization       ' and CCDA-TITLE02 is '              CardDemo                  ', both PIC X(40) - and the '  Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)   ' line above it is commented out with an asterisk in column 7, so line 22 is the active value. CCDA-THANK-YOU of the same copybook and CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU of app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy are different constants of different widths and neither is used here; only the PF3 arm at :88-90 sends one.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at offset 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then the named SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and is never hand-padded into the rows, so the rows here are the job's bytes and nothing else. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster it loads; KEYS(8,0) is also why the eight-character key of :215-216 addresses the whole of SEC-USR-ID and nothing beyond it. All ten rows are seeded even though the lookup misses: against an empty dataset the miss would be trivially true and would not distinguish the correct key from a broken one, whereas against these ten it distinguishes ZZZZ9999 from every key the file does hold.

expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl contains no WRITE, no REWRITE and no DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. The ten expectedFinalState images therefore also assert that a rejected sign-on leaves the security file exactly as it found it - no failed-attempt counter, no lock-out flag, no audit row, none of which the COBOL writes and none of which may be added - and each is pinned at the full eighty characters, so a record that omitted SEC-USR-FILLER would be short by exactly 23. The dataset-level expectation adds the row count and the record width on top, so a dataset that lost or gained a row is caught even where no row-level image would notice. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 and the FILE definition in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD - and never by a dataset name. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0: an online transaction sets none, and zero is stated as the observation rather than left to a default.

Determinism. The clock is pinned at 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it, and it is genuinely consumed here rather than merely declared: :179 moves FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE into WS-CURDATE-DATA and :181-197 renders CURDATEO as 07/19/22 in the MM/DD/YY order the three MOVEs of :186-190 build, and CURTIMEO as the nine-character '23:12:33 ' - eight characters of HH:MM:SS in a PIC X(9) receiver, so the ninth byte is a space and the width is not eight. APPLIDO and SYSIDO come from the two EXEC CICS ASSIGN calls at :198-204, for which there is no CICS here; CICSAWS1 and AWS1 are substituted for them, identical across all twenty cases and pinned so that a translation which invented a region name would be caught. AWS1 is a four-character system identifier in a PIC X(8) item, so it is pinned space-padded to eight. The charset is named US-ASCII explicitly, because the ASCII fixtures are US-ASCII and the platform default is never relied on. Nothing here reads a wall clock and nothing is random.

Two deviations recorded rather than quietly worked around. First, app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:59 is *COPY DFHATTR. with the asterisk in column 7, which makes it a COBOL comment, so no DFHATTR attribute constant applies to this program however many other programs copy that member. Second, COSGN00C never copies CSSETATY - its only consumer is COACTUPC - so there is no DFHRED plus '*' highlight applied at run time and no xxxC, xxxP, xxxH or xxxV item is assigned anywhere; the attributes map of the send is empty for exactly that reason, and it is empty as an assertion rather than as an omission. What marks the error on this screen instead is the cursor request on USERIDL together with ERRMSG's own static map properties, ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) with COLOR=RED at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:197-200, which are properties of the map definition and not of anything the program moves. Where a run-time attribute value would come from is common/BmsAttributes, which reproduces DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR from IBM CICS documentation because both are IBM-supplied and absent from this checkout, as DFHAID is too - which is also why the attention identifier is named here by its common/CicsAid mnemonic DFHENTER and never as a raw byte.

The security posture is unchanged in both directions. The ten seeded rows keep their legacy plaintext SEC-USR-PWD span byte for byte, and the typed password travels in the clear, because that is what :223 compares; digesting either side would need Spring Security, which is out of scope, and would change which requests sign on, which is forbidden. Nothing is interposed anywhere in this case: no credential store, no digest, no issued session credential and no security filter chain. The typed password is in fact the correct one, and the request is still refused - because the key never matched, so :223 is never evaluated. That the program answers 'User not found' here and 'Wrong Password' at :242-243 is a legacy information-disclosure property, distinguishing a non-existent user from a wrong password for anyone who can read the screen; it is preserved exactly as the source has it, is not endorsed, and must not be unified into one message for tidiness.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for the two titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes and widths, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00 and the USRSEC file, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand, and the substitution is escalated rather than absorbed.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path - which is what puts the decision logic within reach of a branch assertion. Of the three arms of :221-257 this case is the not-found one, and of the two ways to reach it from the data it is the case-differing key rather than the short key that case18 holds or the wholly unknown upper-case key of case05. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c 'GO TO' and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked here. DUPKEY, DUPREC and ENDFILE are unreachable from this program, whose only file operation is that single keyed READ, so none of them is fabricated either.

One change of coverage is recorded rather than left to be discovered. This slot previously held a second wrong-password case, typing a password of the seeded width differing from it in a single character; the build prompt reassigns case17 to the key-normalisation-on-a-miss scenario above, so that behaviour moves out of the slot. The wrong-password ELSE at :241-246 remains covered - by case04 and case14, which type a password of the same eight-character width that differs from the seeded one, and by case15, which types a strict prefix of it and must still be refused, which is what forbids a comparison that trims or compares a prefix - and the plaintext byte-for-byte gate takes its negative witnesses from those cases and its positive witness from case02, which types the seeded password exactly and signs on. No user-specified rules exist for this project - review_rules returns the single line 'No user rules provided' - so none is cited here; the enterprise practices the plan substitutes for them are what this fixture is held to, and their absence is not treated as licence to assert less.
